## What changed
Branch `feature/hardening-audit-and-landing-refresh` has no upstream, so the review scope is the union of (a) 20 files already committed vs `main` (merge-base `8febbc9`) and (b) 13 tracked files with uncommitted working-tree changes vs `HEAD`, plus (c) several untracked new files not visible to `git diff` at all. Committed work (main...HEAD) is infrastructure/hardening: adds a second Vercel "oci" container service (`containers/function/{Dockerfile,server.mjs,path.mjs}` + tests + `.dockerignore` + `scripts/push-vcr-function-image.ps1`), deletes the shadowing `next.config.js` so the CSP-bearing `next.config.ts` is active again, updates `vercel.json`/`middleware.ts` to route/exclude `/oci`, tightens `app/api/github-repo/route.ts` (SSRF/rate-limit hardening, per repo CLAUDE.md history) with a new test file, adds a `profiles` RLS migration, and touches `.env.example`/README/package.json/apple-icon/two test files. Uncommitted working-tree changes layer further security/config work on top: RLS-related edits to `app/api/lead/route.ts`, `app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts`, `app/api/intercom/jwt/route.ts`, `lib/actions/work-orders.ts`, admin pages, `vercel.json`, `.gitignore`, and a large rewrite of `PLAN.md`/`CLAUDE.md`; it also **deletes** `components/landing/Proof.tsx` and heavily trims `pnpm-lock.yaml`/`package.json` (dependency removal — verify nothing still imports the deleted component or removed deps). Untracked-but-real additions that `git diff` won't surface: a brand-new `app/api/cron/` route + test, a second RLS migration (`20260717064702_rls_hardening_wo_and_anon_insert.sql`), a stray `package-lock.json` (project is pnpm-only per CLAUDE.md — likely accidental and worth flagging), plus agent-tooling noise (`.claude/`, `.claude-flow/`, `.swarm/`, `$c`, `'`, `repo-snapshot.tar.gz`) that is not reviewable code and should be excluded/gitignored rather than reviewed.

CLAUDE.md conventions a reviewer should apply: (1) repo-root CLAUDE.md flags the exact duplicate-config trap this branch fixes — Next.js loads `next.config.js` before `.ts`, so deleting the `.js` file is the correct fix but confirm no other code still assumes the old slim config; (2) `/api/lead`, `/api/webhooks/stripe`, `/api/webhooks/calendly`, and admin routes must stay `force-dynamic`/`nodejs` runtime per the architecture notes — check the Stripe webhook diff didn't touch `runtime = "nodejs"`; (3) any new third-party host touched by the cron/webhook changes needs a matching CSP entry in `next.config.ts`; (4) `lib/database.types.ts` must never be hand-edited (regenerate via `pnpm db:types`) — check if RLS migrations require a regen; (5) package manager is pnpm only (`packageManager: pnpm@10.34.1`) — the untracked `package-lock.json` violates this; (6) global user CLAUDE.md mandates a security-reviewer-agent pass and a `pnpm run build && pnpm test`-equivalent (`pnpm verify`) before calling RLS/auth changes done, plus no hardcoded secrets and Zod input validation at boundaries (`app/api/lead/route.ts` pattern) for the new `app/api/cron/route.ts`; (7) per repo CLAUDE.md, `components/landing/Proof.tsx` deletion must be cross-checked against `app/page.tsx`/other landing composers for dangling imports.

## Conventions
(none noted)

Run the diff command above and review through EACH of the following cleanup lenses:

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.


### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.


### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.


### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.


### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Surface up to 30 candidate findings, each with file, line, a one-line summary, and a concrete failure_scenario — the user-visible consequence (error, wrong output, data loss), not an intermediate state (value stale, set grows). Cover whichever lenses apply — you do not need findings from every lens; prioritize the highest-cost issues across all of them. Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — do not silently drop half-believed candidates; an independent verifier judges them next. If nothing qualifies, return an empty list.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud).
